label: Calendar
mood: the date shown on a calendar — a month sheet set in fine rules and numerals with the event day marked by a filled disc (a run of days by a capped band), a daily tear-off block (일력) with month and day set large together, or the strip of the event's week with the day picked out in a pill. Drawn in the poster's own faces in two or three flat inks, so it is vector and changes voice with the type theme, from a Swiss grotesque to a 명조. Reads the date (and a range) from the event information. Good for anything people must put in their diary: services and church events, school and community days, openings, deadlines, seasonal events, conferences.

paper.note: month: none (drawn straight on the page in rules and numerals) | sheet (on a sheet of paper, slightly turned, with a soft shadow)

weekStart.note: sun | mon — the first column of the month sheet and the week strip

month.note: a month sheet: month and year as the header, the weekday row and the days, the event day on a filled disc (a run of days on a band capped at both ends), Sundays in the accent

tearoff.note: a daily tear-off block (일력): binding strip with two rings, the month and the day set large together (11.15), the weekday below, page edges showing underneath, slightly turned

week.note: the seven days of the event's week, weekday letters over day numbers, the event day in a tall pill — a wide, low image for bands of art
